definition: 'Being' said of everything with one and the same ratio, so that all beings fall on one homogeneous scale of a common nature (one comparative of being on one domain, of which God and creatures would be grades).
note: Recorded for contrast: it is the sense that ST I q.13 a.5 (neither univocally) and q.3 a.5 ad 2 (God is no proportioned, homogeneous measure) deny, and the sense under which being would be a genus. A univocity source (for example Scotus, Ordinatio I d.3) would source it if it is ever argued for as a rival; none is pinned.
